name: Salicylic acid

lead: Salicylic acid is a beta hydroxy acid derived from willow bark chemistry and used in washes, toners and spot treatments for acne, blackheads and oily skin, as well as in treatments for warts, dandruff and keratosis pilaris.
Its oil solubility lets it work inside pores, which makes it a standard over-the-counter acne ingredient at concentrations up to a few percent.

paras: Salicylic acid is a keratolytic that loosens the bonds between corneocytes and dissolves intercellular lipids in clogged follicles, helping clear comedones. It also has mild anti-inflammatory effects.

Dryness, peeling and irritation are common. Large-area or high-strength use can cause salicylate absorption and toxicity, so caution is advised in children, in pregnancy and over broken skin. Photosensitivity is mild but sunscreen is sensible.
